div.fw: A Plowmān · A Rebe · A Myller A Sompnour A ꝐPerdoner͗ A Maunicipull And Chaucers
div.l: But hit were · Any ꝑpersoūn obstynatt
What so he were of hiȝe or lowe estate
Hym wolde he snybbe scharpely for the nones
A Bett̉er preste y trowe nowher͗ none ys
He wayted aftur · no pompe ne reủerence
Ne maked hym a spysed conscyens
But crystes lore and his aposteles twelve
He taught but furst he folowed hyt hȳm selve
¶ With hym þ̉er was plowman his broder
That had y ladde of donge many a fother
And a trewe swynker and a gode was he
Lyuynge in pees and in ꝑperfite charyte
At all tymes þough he gamed or smerte
God loued he best with all his herte
And þan his neyȝtbur ryght as hym selve
He wold thressch and þ̉er to dyke and delve
For crystes sake for eủery pore wyght
With oute hir͗ yf hit lay in his myght
His tythes payd he fayre and well
Both of his proper swynke ⁊and his catell
In a tabard he rode up on a mere
¶ There was also a Reve and a myller
A Sompnour͗ and a pardoner also
A Mauncypull and my self þ̉er was no mo
The myller was a stoute carle for þe nones
Full bygge he was of Brawn and bones
That proued well for oủer all þ̉er he com̄
At wrastelynge he wold haue awey þe Ram̄
He was schorte schulderd a thykke knarr͗
The nas no dor͗ þᵗat he ne wold heve of harr͗
Or breke hit with rennyng with his hede
Hys berde as any sowe or foxe was rede·
